items.title: Two Colorado Law Enforcement Officers Honored by the Attorney General
items.summary: DENVER – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Colorado announces that Sergeant Donnie Smith of the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office and Deputy John Gray of the Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office have been honored by the Department of Justice with the Honor the Honorable: Attorney General’s Award for Distinguished Service in Policing.

items.title: DOJ Scores Key Victory in Precedent-Setting Military Attorney Licensing Case
items.summary: The Justice Department has defeated New Mexico’s attempt to dismiss a landmark case involving the licensing of servicemember and military spouse attorneys. On Nov. 19, Judge Kea Riggs of the U.S. District for the District of New Mexico denied motions to dismiss filed by the New Mexico Supreme Court and the New Mexico Board of Bar Examiners in the Department’s first-ever lawsuit to enforce the professional license portability provisions of the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA).

items.title: EFF to Congress: Mass Surveillance Is Too Important to Shove into Must-Pass Bill
items.summary: In June 2026, the surveillance authority Section 702 of FISA expired absent a consensus among lawmakers over the terms of its reauthorization . Now, with the program set to truly turn off within the next few months, surveillance hawks and national security maximalists are rushing to renew this secretive power by shoving it into a must-pass bill, like a continuing resolution to fund the government or the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) or an end of year, rushed, funding bill to prevent a shutdown. This would be both undemocratic and suppress any real chance at reform. In an effort to prevent that, EFF has singed into a letter with over 25 civil liberties organizations, including the ACLU, Color of Change, and the Brennan Center, to urge Congress not to allow such a significant and dangerous program to be tacked onto a must-pass bill. The letter says: “The NDAA is among the most important bills Congress considers each year. It should not be used as a vehicle to circumvent or to cut short this long-running bipartisan debate over Americans’ civil liberties and constitutional rights, nor to force lawmakers to choose between supporting our national defense and ending warrantles
